title: Project portfolio composition from a solution design

description.need: A solution design that never becomes projects is a drawing. The step from one to the other is where portfolios go wrong quietly: a service in the design that nobody created a home for, a repository that exists on disk but was never registered so no persona can reach it, a project standing with no owner because adoption was left for later, two projects that both believe they own the same context, and a project created with no goal at all, whose team then invents its own direction from whatever it can see.
description.input: The current solution design with its contexts, services, data owners and exclusions; the workspace as it stands, with whatever projects, repositories and App Masters already exist in it; and the charters and recipes available to adopt.
description.coreAction: Turn the design into a portfolio that matches it: create each missing repository and register it as a project in the workspace in one act, adopt an App Master on each with the charters that context actually needs, set each project's first goals from the design's own words, then read the portfolio back against the design and resolve every orphan, every duplicate owner and every project standing without direction.
description.output: A workspace whose projects correspond one to one with the design's contexts, each with a real repository, an App Master holding named charters, and first goals traceable to a line of the design; plus a reconciliation note listing what was created, what already existed, and every mismatch that could not be resolved and who has to decide it.

activities.label: Compare the design's contexts against the projects the workspace already holds
Decide which contexts become projects now, which wait, and which existing project already covers one
Create each missing repository and register it as a project in the workspace in one act
Adopt an App Master on each project with the charters its context needs
Set each project's first goals from the design rather than from the project's own guess
Read the portfolio back against the design and name every orphan, duplicate owner and unowned project
Write what was created, what was left alone, and what a person has to decide

outcomes.statement: Every service the design names has a project, or is recorded as deliberately deferred.
successCriteria: Each context in the current design maps to exactly one project in the workspace, by name
A context deliberately not created carries the reason and what would change that
A project that exists with no context behind it is named as an orphan rather than tolerated

outcomes.statement: Every project created has a repository that exists and is registered, so work can start in it the same day.
successCriteria: Each new project has a repository on disk under version control and a registration the platform can resolve
A repository created but not registered, or registered but missing on disk, is treated as a failure of this work rather than as a later problem
Creating the same project twice changes nothing, so a rerun after a partial failure is safe

outcomes.statement: No project stands in the workspace without an App Master holding named charters.
successCriteria: Each project has exactly one App Master, and the charters it holds are listed
The charters given match what that context actually does rather than being the same set everywhere
A project whose adoption failed is reported unowned rather than counted as created

outcomes.statement: Every project starts with goals a reader can trace back to a line of the design.
successCriteria: Each project has at least one goal, and each goal names the part of the design it serves
A goal that cannot be traced to the design is either removed or the design is revised to carry it
A project left without goals is named in the report as needing direction, never left silent

outcomes.statement: No two projects claim the same context, and no context is claimed by none.
successCriteria: The reconciliation lists context to project as a one to one mapping with the exceptions called out
A duplicate claim is resolved by moving the responsibility, and the design is updated to say where it now lives
An unresolvable conflict is escalated with both claims and the evidence, rather than settled by whichever project asked last

guidance: Create the project and the repository in one act; a repository nobody registered is invisible and a project with no repository has nowhere to build. One context, one project, one App Master, and if two projects would touch the same data one of them is wrong. Give each App Master the charters its context needs rather than the full set. Set the first goals from the design so the project starts pointed somewhere, then read the portfolio as a whole for the service nobody took.

connectorRoles.note: the workspace door where projects are registered, App Masters adopted and goals set
where each new repository is created and from where an existing one is read

recommendedTrigger.rationale: A design change is the real trigger: a context added, split or removed is exactly the moment the portfolio stops matching, and composing before then produces projects nobody asked for. A self paced fallback earns its place beside it, because the portfolio also drifts without any design change at all, through a failed adoption or a repository that was moved by hand, and only a periodic reconciliation finds those.

personalizationNeeds: Where new repositories are allowed to be created on this machine or host, since creating one in the wrong place is not reversible by the same work that created it
What a new repository must contain before it counts as created here, for example a readme, a licence, a project marker or a first commit
Which charters exist and which of them an App Master should hold by default, because handing every project the full set is the same as handing it none
How far this work may go without asking, from proposing the portfolio through to creating repositories and adopting owners, since creation is not a reversible act
Whether an existing project may be re bound to a different context, or whether that is always a person's decision
dependencies: a current solution design to compose from, since a portfolio composed from memory is what this work exists to prevent
a workspace that already exists and can hold projects
a one step repository and project creation door, because creating the two separately is the failure mode this work is written against

examples.title: The Personas workspace as the workspace role
examples.notes: Personas is the platform this recipe was authored against, and it carries the whole door: a create route that git inits a repository under the dedicated root and registers it as a project in one call, an App Master adoption door that creates the project team, KPIs, triggers and mandate charter together, and goal routes that hang goals off a milestone. There is no connector catalogue entry for it, so adoption binds the workspace role to whatever surface holds the portfolio; project_management is the honest type for it because the door is projects, owners and goals rather than documents.

examples.title: The codebase connector as the repository_host role
examples.notes: builtin-codebase reaches a registered checkout, which is what makes a newly created repository usable by the App Master that was just adopted onto it. The ordering matters: create and register first, adopt second, because an adoption onto a project whose root path does not exist fails in a way that leaves the project standing and unowned.

examples.title: A six project bank portfolio from one design
examples.notes: A design separating a bank into core ledger, contracts, lending, investments, edge and platform becomes six projects, and the reconciliation is where the value shows: the platform project has no business context of its own and exists only because queues, infrastructure and the load harness need an owner, which is exactly the kind of project a mechanical one to one mapping from contexts would never create.

inputSchema.name: workspace_id
inputSchema.description: The workspace whose portfolio is being composed. Every project created or reconciled belongs to it.

inputSchema.name: design_ref
inputSchema.description: Pointer to the solution design version being composed from. Empty means read the current design from wherever the design_home role is bound.

inputSchema.name: dry_run
inputSchema.description: Produce the reconciliation and the plan without creating repositories, projects or adoptions. Useful on the first pass, where the plan is the thing a person wants to see.
